subject: Private VPC Pricing — next steps & token volumes
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@enterprisecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@enterprisecorp.com>
Cc: Sandeep Mehta <sandeep@enterprisecorp.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Private VPC pricing questions

Thanks again for the call this morning — good conversation. A quick recap and a few follow-ups from our side so we can get a ballpark for procurement: 

Recap / asks from EnterpriseCorp: 
- Deployment: Private VPC (customer-managed VPC) + on-prem option for one subset of data flows.
- Environments: we anticipate dev, staging, prod initially (3 envs). Might add a second prod region later.
- Expected token volume: initial launch ~300M tokens/month, with growth to ~800M tokens/month in 12 months.
- Quality target: want same inference profile as hosted; will consider quantization options if unit economics improve.
- Support: prefer enterprise support with 24/7 escalation for prod.

Questions we need for procurement: 
1) Licensing model for Private/VPC: annual license vs perpetual + maintenance? Any minimums?
2) Unit economics: target $/1M tokens for committed volumes (what ranges do you recommend for committed tiers vs overage?)
3) Environment fees: pricing for additional environments (staging/dev/prod count).
4) Onboarding: estimated timeline and one-time professional services estimate.

Budget guidance: procurement asked for a target ARR range to evaluate approval — our internal range is $150k–$250k ARR but we can be flexible if the unit economics and committed volume discounts line up.

Can you send a short options sheet (rough numbers are fine) so we can move to procurement review? Appreciate it — Alex

--
Alex Johnson
Head of Product, Enterprise Integrations
EnterpriseCorp
alex.johnson@enterprisecorp.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@enterprisecorp.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@enterprisecorp.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Private VPC pricing questions

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and the budget range. Leaving Ben and Rachel on copy to validate numbers, but below is a concise set of options that align with what we discussed. Attaching a one-page pricing overview and a SOW template for procurement to review.

Option A — Standard Private (recommended for initial prod)
- Licensing: Annual platform license for Private deployment. Example starting point: $140,000/year for 1 production environment (includes dev/staging at a reduced environment fee).
- Token economics: committed pricing example: $120 per 1M tokens for committed volumes up to 500M tokens/month. Overage pricing: $180 per 1M tokens.
- Environments: base license includes 1 prod + dev/staging (limited). Additional full environments: $20,000/environment/year.
- Support: Standard (business hours) included; Enterprise support is an add-on.
- Onboarding/PS: one-time estimate $25–40k depending on integration complexity. Typical timeline 4–8 weeks.

Option B — Enterprise Private (for EnterpriseCorp scale and 24/7)
- Licensing: $220,000/year base license for single production environment.
- Token economics (committed): $80–$100 per 1M tokens for commitments >= 500M tokens/month (tiered). Overage: $140 per 1M tokens.
- Environments: additional environment $25,000/env/year.
- Support: Enterprise (24/7, dedicated TAM, SLA) included in license or as a +20% add-on.
- Onboarding/PS: $40–75k depending on custom connectors and compliance evidence. Timeline 6–10 weeks.

Notes / next steps:
- These are ballpark figures to get procurement moving. Final pricing will depend on committed token volume, number of environments, and whether you want on-prem included in the license or billed as a separate engineering engagement.
- If you confirm committed month 1 and 12-month growth plan (e.g., 300M -> 800M), we can run a model showing ARR, unit $/1M at each tier and produce a formal quote for procurement + draft MSA.

I attached: Redwood_Private_Pricing_Overview.pdf (1-pager) and SOW-template.docx.

Would tomorrow (Tue) at 11am PT for a short procurement pricing call work?

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Exec, Strategic Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | (408) 555-0199

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Sandeep Mehta <sandeep@enterprisecorp.com>, Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@enterprisecorp.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Private VPC pricing questions

Looping in a couple quick recommendations based on scale:

1) Licensing model: for EnterpriseCorp size I recommend Enterprise Private approach. Offer a 12-month committed contract with tiered committed pricing at 500M/month threshold. That maps to better unit economics and predictable capacity.

2) Suggested baseline numbers (for internal approval):
- Base license: $200,000/year (includes 1 prod environment, dev/staging tooling access).
- Committed token tiers: 
  - 0–100M/mo: $160 per 1M tokens
  - 100–500M/mo: $110 per 1M tokens
  - 500M+ (committed): $85 per 1M tokens
- Overage: +60–80% above committed tier rate (negotiable).
- Additional environments: $25k/env/year (prod-class).
- Enterprise support: +20% of license (or included for top-tier deals).

3) PS/onboarding: estimate $45k for security/compliance onboarding (SOC2 evidence review, private install checklist) if they require on-prem or extra controls.

These numbers give procurement clear traded options: lower base license + higher $/1M vs higher base + lower unit economics.

Happy to sync if you want to tighten the ranges before we send a formal quote.

\u0012Ben
Ben Carter | Head of Sales, Enterprise | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | (650) 555-0133

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Private VPC pricing questions

Alex — thanks, Ben — appreciate the options. Below is a short, procurement-friendly summary (we'll convert this into a formal PDF quote once you confirm the committed volumes + env count).

Summary options (procurement-friendly)
A) Mid-range enterprise option (recommended for predictable growth)
- Base license: $200k/year (1 prod environments included)
- Committed pricing: $110 per 1M tokens (applies up to 500M/mo).
- Additional tokens above committed tiers: $160 per 1M tokens.
- Additional envs: $25k/year each.
- Enterprise support: +20% (recommended) -> $40k/year add-on.
- One-time onboarding PS: $40k estimate.

B) Higher-commitment discount (best unit economics)
- Base license: $220k/year
- Committed pricing: $85 per 1M tokens for commitments >= 500M/mo
- Additional envs: $25k/year each
- Enterprise support: included or as negotiated
- PS: $50–75k

Next steps I recommend from procurement side:
1) Confirm: committed month 1 volume (300M) and target 12-month committed baseline (e.g., 600–800M).
2) Confirm: number of prod-class environments (you mentioned 3 total; clarify how many are prod-class vs dev).
3) Confirm: desire for on-prem option in scope of license vs separate engagement.

If you can confirm the three items above I will:
- Prepare an itemized quote and a draft MSA for legal redline.
- Schedule a procurement call tomorrow at 11am PT if that still works.

Would you like me to include a cost model showing $/1M tokens vs committed volume for the 300–800M range?

Thanks — looking forward to moving this to procurement.

Marissa
Account Executive, Strategic Sales | Redwood Inference

Marissa — thanks, that is helpful and within the ballpark. A few confirmations from procurement/finance: 
- Confirmed initial committed volume: 300M tokens/month. Procurement is willing to discuss a baseline commitment of 600M/month for 12 months if unit economics are favorable.
- Environments: 3 total — 1 prod-class, 1 staging (prod-like), 1 dev (non-prod). We consider the staging environment prod-like and would expect full parity for testing.
- Support: enterprise support required for prod/staging (24/7).
- Budget: finance still prefers to see an itemized ARR; they are comfortable evaluating $150k–$250k ARR but will stretch to $350k if the committed pricing is favorable.

Next asks: please send an itemized quote showing the Mid-range enterprise option and Higher-commitment discount option with the following:
- Breakdown: license, token commitments (show $/1M at 300M and at 600M committed), additional env fees, enterprise support fee, one-time PS.
- Include a proposed timeline for onboarding and a draft MSA to start legal review.

We can take the procurement call tomorrow 11am PT — Alex + Sandeep + procurement lead will join.

Thanks — Alex
